summary: This short document updates RFC 7854, the BGP Monitoring Protocol, by changing registration procedures for several registries. Any BMP registry with a range of 32768-65530 marked Specification Required now has that range set to First Come First Served.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 9515 changes how a range of values is registered in six BGP Monitoring Protocol registries. The range moves from Specification Required to First Come First Served to lower the barrier to registering code points.

subtitle: Changes the registration policy for a range in six BMP registries.

tldr.problem: Several BMP registries used Specification Required for code points 32768-65530, a policy whose practical difference from Standards Action was smaller than expected and that could encourage unregistered use.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC changes that range to First Come First Served in six BMP registries.
tldr.outcome: RFC 9515 updates RFC 7854 by revising registration procedures; it does not change the underlying BMP security issues.

facts.label: Registration policy change
facts.value: Specification Required to First Come First Served

today: RFC 9515 is a Proposed Standard from December 2023 and updates RFC 7854.

sections.title: Why BMP Registration Rules Changed
sections.content:
RFC 7854 created several BMP registries with a 32768-65530 range designated Specification Required. The RFC 9515 introduction says later experience showed less practical difference between Specification Required and Standards Action than theory suggests.

It also says a low registration barrier is desirable to reduce the risk of conflicts from unregistered code points, sometimes called code point squatting.
sections.plainLanguage: Some BMP values had a registration rule that was not much lighter in practice than a full standards process. The RFC lowers the barrier to reduce informal use of unregistered values.

sections.title: Six Registries and the New Policy
sections.content:
The changed registries are BMP Statistics Types; BMP Initiation and Peer Up Information TLVs; BMP Termination Message TLVs; BMP Termination Message Reason Codes; BMP Route Mirroring TLVs; and BMP Route Mirroring Information Codes.

In each registry, the range 32768-65530 changes from Specification Required to First Come First Served. The RFC does not describe other ranges as changing.
sections.plainLanguage: Six BMP registries change their policy for values 32768 through 65530. Those values are now registered First Come First Served instead of Specification Required.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC says that revising the registration procedures does not change the underlying security issues inherent in RFC 7854.
sections.plainLanguage: The registration policy changes, but the RFC says BMP's underlying security issues do not change.
